title: Headless & Automation
description: Run Claude without the chat UI: claude -p, output formats, pipes, scripts and CI.

lessons.title: claude -p Basics
lessons.description: One prompt in, one answer out

theory.title: Print mode
theory.body:
`claude -p "query"` (long form `--print`) runs Claude **non-interactively**: it does the task, prints the result, and exits.

It reads **stdin**, so you can pipe data in and redirect the answer out like any Unix tool.

It exits with code `0` on success and non-zero on failure, so scripts can branch on it. Kip calls this "going headless" (the shell stays on).
theory.code:
claude -p "What does the auth module do?"

cat build-error.txt | claude -p "concisely explain the root cause" > output.txt

# keep going in the most recent conversation
claude -c -p "Now check for type errors"

theory.title: Output formats
theory.body:
`--output-format` controls the shape of the output:

`text` (default): plain text.

`json`: one JSON object with the answer in `result` plus metadata like `session_id` and `total_cost_usd`.

`stream-json`: newline-delimited JSON events as they happen (pair it with `--verbose`).

exercises.prompt: Run Claude non-interactively with the prompt "summarize this project".
exercises.hint: claude plus the print flag, then the prompt in quotes.
exercises.explanation: `-p` / `--print` runs a single prompt headlessly and prints the result.

exercises.prompt: Pipe the contents of logs.txt into Claude with the prompt "explain these errors".
exercises.explanation: Print mode reads stdin, so piped content becomes part of what Claude sees.

exercises.prompt: Which output format streams newline-delimited JSON events in real time?
exercises.explanation: `--output-format stream-json` emits one JSON event per line as the run progresses.

exercises.prompt: Get JSON output and extract just the answer text with jq.
exercises.explanation: With `--output-format json`, the response text lives in the `result` field.

exercises.prompt: Match each flag value to what you get.
exercises.explanation: Pick text for humans, json for scripts, stream-json for live progress, and --json-schema for a fixed shape.

exercises.prompt: Continue your most recent conversation headlessly with the prompt "Now focus on the database queries".
accepted: claude -c -p "Now focus on the database queries"
claude --continue -p "Now focus on the database queries"
claude -c --print "Now focus on the database queries"
claude --continue --print "Now focus on the database queries"
claude -p "Now focus on the database queries" --continue
claude -p "Now focus on the database queries" -c
exercises.hint: Combine the continue flag with the print flag.
exercises.explanation: `-c` / `--continue` works with `-p`, so a script can send follow-ups to the same conversation.

exercises.prompt: In `--output-format json`, which field reports the estimated spend for the run?
exercises.explanation: The JSON payload includes `total_cost_usd`, a client-side estimate scripts can track.

exercises.prompt: How can a shell script tell whether a `claude -p` run failed?
options: Parse the word 'error' from the output
Check the exit code: 0 on success, non-zero on failure
exercises.explanation: Claude Code exits 0 on success and non-zero when the run fails, so `if`/`&&` work as usual.

exercises.prompt: A script pipes a failed build log into Claude and saves the answer for the team.
options: cat build.log | claude -p "concisely explain the root cause of this build error and name the file to fix"
exercises.explanation: Nobody can answer follow-up questions in a script, so the prompt must say exactly what output you want.

theory.title: Guardrails for unattended runs
theory.body:
Nobody is around to click "allow" in a script, so decide permissions up front.

`--allowedTools` pre-approves tools, using permission rule syntax like `Bash(git diff *)`. `--disallowedTools` denies or removes them.

`--max-turns N` caps agentic turns (print mode only). `--append-system-prompt` adds instructions while keeping Claude Code's defaults. `--bare` skips auto-discovered hooks, plugins, MCP servers and CLAUDE.md for reproducible CI runs.

Use `--dangerously-skip-permissions` only inside an isolated container.
theory.code:
claude -p "Run the test suite and fix any failures" \
  --allowedTools "Bash,Read,Edit" --max-turns 10

theory.title: Claude in GitHub Actions
theory.body:
The `anthropics/claude-code-action` runs Claude in your workflows. Mention `@claude` in an issue or PR comment and it gets to work.

Fastest setup: run `/install-github-app` inside a session. It installs the Claude GitHub App, saves your key as a repo secret (like `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), and prepares the workflow PR.

Pass CLI flags through the `claude_args` input.
theory.code:
- uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
  with:
    anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
    claude_args: "--max-turns 5"

exercises.prompt: Headlessly run the prompt "Run the test suite and fix any failures", pre-approving the tools "Bash,Read,Edit".
accepted: claude -p "Run the test suite and fix any failures" --allowedTools "Bash,Read,Edit"
claude --print "Run the test suite and fix any failures" --allowedTools "Bash,Read,Edit"
claude -p "Run the test suite and fix any failures" --allowed-tools "Bash,Read,Edit"
claude --print "Run the test suite and fix any failures" --allowed-tools "Bash,Read,Edit"
exercises.explanation: `--allowedTools` lets listed tools run without a permission prompt, which a script can't answer.

exercises.prompt: Headlessly run the prompt "fix the lint errors", limited to 3 agentic turns.
exercises.explanation: `--max-turns` caps how many agentic turns a print-mode run can take before it stops with an error.

exercises.prompt: Complete review.sh: security-review a PR diff and return JSON.
exercises.code:
gh pr diff "$1" | claude ___ \
  --___ "You are a security engineer. Review for vulnerabilities." \
  --output-format ___
exercises.explanation: Print mode reads the piped diff, `--append-system-prompt` adds the reviewer role, and json makes it scriptable.

options: Append keeps Claude Code's default prompt and adds yours; --system-prompt replaces it entirely
Append only works in interactive mode
--system-prompt adds text to the end of every user message
exercises.explanation: Appending preserves the default tool and safety guidance; replacing drops all of it.

exercises.prompt: Match each flag to its job in a script.
exercises.explanation: These flags make unattended runs predictable: what Claude may do, how long, and with which instructions.

exercises.prompt: Inside a session, start the quick setup for Claude in GitHub Actions.
exercises.explanation: `/install-github-app` installs the app, saves the secret, and prepares the workflow PR.

options: On your laptop, to save time
Inside an isolated container or sandbox with nothing valuable to damage
exercises.explanation: It skips every permission check, so only use it where mistakes can't touch real systems or secrets.

exercises.prompt: Order the quick setup for @claude in GitHub.
steps: Install the gh CLI and run gh auth login
Open claude in the repo and run /install-github-app
Let it install the Claude GitHub App and save the secret
Create and merge the workflow pull request it prepares
Mention @claude in an issue or PR comment
exercises.explanation: Setup needs gh first; once the workflow PR is merged, @claude mentions trigger runs.

exercises.code:
- uses: anthropics/___@v1
  with:
    anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
    claude_args: "--___ 5"
exercises.explanation: The action is anthropics/claude-code-action, and CLI flags like --max-turns go in claude_args.

exercises.scenario: A nightly CI job pipes `npm test` output into `claude -p`. Write the prompt so the report is useful with nobody around to ask follow-ups.
exercises.sample: npm test 2>&1 | claude -p "These are CI test results. For each failing test, give the test name, the likely root cause in one sentence, and the file to look at. Output Markdown bullets only. If every test passed, print exactly: ALL GREEN"
exercises.explanation: Headless prompts must define the exact output format, including what to print when there's nothing to report.

mission.title: Go Headless
mission.intro: Kip unplugs the chat window. Make Claude work as a plain command-line tool in your own scripts.
checklist: Run claude -p "summarize this project" in a repo
Pipe input: git log --oneline -20 | claude -p "summarize these recent commits"
Run a prompt with --output-format json and pipe it to jq -r '.result'
Optional: run /install-github-app in a repo you admin
mission.explanation: Print mode, pipes, JSON output and guardrail flags are the building blocks of every Claude automation.

cheatsheet.description: Run one prompt non-interactively, print, exit (also --print).
Pipe content into Claude via stdin.
Continue the most recent conversation headlessly.
Plain text, one JSON object, or streamed JSON events.
Deny or remove tools for the run.
Limit agentic turns in print mode.
Add instructions while keeping the default system prompt.
Skip auto-discovered config for faster, reproducible scripted runs.
Set up Claude in GitHub Actions for this repo.
Mention in an issue or PR comment to trigger the action.
